sections.title: Prerequisite: The Area Interpretation of Determinants
lecture_lines: The determinant equals the parallelogram's area.
Scaling one column scales the total area.
Transforming vectors morphs the base square.
animations: Create a square [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/square.svg] with area 1.0 using color #FFFFFF.
Transform square into a parallelogram [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/parallelogram.svg], keeping area color #FF00FF.
Label the area of the parallelogram [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/parallelogram.svg] as 'det(A)' using #FFFF00.

sections.title: Framing the Linear System as Vector Addition
lecture_lines: Systems represent vector additions: x1*v1 + x2*v2 = b.
Imagine vectors as motors steering a drone.
Finding x1 and x2 guides the drone.
animations: Draw basis vectors i and j as arrows in #00FF00. [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/drone.svg]
Draw vector v = x*i + y*j using arrows in #00FFFF.
Animate adding x*i and y*j to form vector v.

sections.title: Visualizing Cramer's Rule: The Area Ratio
lecture_lines: Area of (b, v2) scaled yields x1.
Replacing v1 with b shifts the geometry.
The area ratio mirrors the scaling factor.
animations: Highlight the transformed area with determinant det(A) in #FF0000. [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/none.svg]
Overlay a new area representing det(Ax) in #00FF00. [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/none.svg]
Display ratio det(Ax)/det(A) as x coordinate in #FFFF00. [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/none.svg]

sections.title: Synthesizing the Formula
lecture_lines: Formula equals the ratio of stretched areas.
This ratio gives the vector scaling factor.
animations: Display the formula x = det(Ax) / det(A) in #FFFFFF.
Flash x = det(Ax) / det(A) to emphasize the result.
Show the equivalent formula y = det(Ay) / det(A) in #FFFFFF.

sections.title: Conclusion and Geometric Constraints
lecture_lines: Valid only if det(A) is not zero.
Zero area means vectors are collinear.
Division by zero impossible for collinear systems.
animations: Show two vectors becoming collinear as det(A) nears zero.
Display a warning label 'Division by Zero' in #FF0000.
Fade out objects to indicate limits of geometric interpretation.
